key_insight: DMA² shows that distribution matching distillation works better in native pixel-space when it is adapted to RGB-specific behavior, especially by avoiding low-noise matching that overemphasizes local texture. The paper introduces adversarial and anchor losses to make few-step image generation more stable and more faithful in pixel space.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap between modern distribution-matching distillation methods and native RGB image generation, which have mostly been designed around latent diffusion. The paper asks how to better distill pixel-space teachers for fast, high-quality text-to-image synthesis.
method: Revisits distribution matching distillation for pixel-space teachers instead of latent-space-only setups.
Uses diagnostics to show that low-noise RGB matching is dominated by local texture cues, then replaces it with a fixed high-noise matching band.
Adds adversarial and anchor losses to improve realism and preserve alignment during few-step generation.
impact: This matters for practitioners building fast image generators because it offers a more suitable distillation recipe for native RGB models. It can improve sample quality and training stability while reducing dependence on latent-space assumptions.
